newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli analyst gives warning of possible coup.
newsitem.headline: Israeli analyst gives warning of possible coup.

text.p: A leading Israeli strategic analyst said on Wednesday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had cut security officials out of decision-making, raising the chances they could try to topple him.

Professor Zeev Maoz, head of Tel Aviv University's Jaffee Centre for Strategic Studies, said Netanyahu considered senior army officers to be aligned with the former Labour government and was ignoring their political and military assessments.
"If we face an international crisis while a lack of trust pervades between the military and political echelons, there are good reasons to be concerned," Maoz told the newspaper Haaretz.

"The military has no opportunity to play the political game in order to change the situation and therefore the likelihood of a putsch -- an illegal action -- becomes more and more attractive," he said.

Israeli officers have taken part in political decision-making since before the state's founding in 1948 and many have gone into political careers after retiring from the army. Netanyahu's cabinet includes four retired generals.
Netanyahu has accused the former Labour government of politicising the army by involving army officers in Israeli-Arab peace talks.
